name: Morfran

attributes.attribute: a Welsh god or hero and the son of Ceridwen, conceived ugly
brewed herbs to give her ugly son Morfran the world's wisdom
drank some of the brew by accident, absorbing the wisdom and drawing Ceridwen's wrath
escaped the battle of Camlan because everyone mistook him for a devil

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Morfran, also called Morfran fab Tegid, was a Welsh god or hero. He was the son of the great goddess Ceridwen. He was an ugly child. To make up for this, his mother decided that he would become the world's wisest person. She began brewing a collection of herbs that would bring him wisdom. She set her servant boy Gwion to watch the cauldron. Gwion accidentally drank some of the brew. He absorbed the wisdom and brought down Ceridwen's wrath. Welsh myth says little more of Morfran. His ugliness finally proved useful when he escaped the battle of Camlan. Everyone mistook him for a devil. See Afagddu.
objective: Document the Welsh figure Morfran and Ceridwen's cauldron.
key_results: Record Morfran as Ceridwen's ugly son destined to gain wisdom.
Record Gwion's accidental drink of the brew and its consequence.
Record Morfran's escape from Camlan because he was mistaken for a devil.
